page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 45 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Configured with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the system provides 360.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core). It integrates 3216 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 8 drives without attached GPU acceleration. The underlying AMD architecture incorporates 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded processing and cryptographic capability, recording 129,166.19 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 87,474.41 in PassMark CPU score, and 100,636.3 in PassMark CPU encryption. In memory bandwidth benchmarks, the server delivers 6,372.53 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks and 217.44 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks, falling to an average 76.89 GB/sec for 256 MB write blocks. Single-threaded performance exhibits midrange results, scoring 1,877.0 in Geekbench and 2,862.96 in stress-ng single-core tests.

The dense core count and bundled 3,216 GB local NVMe SSD storage offer substantial I/O throughput and multi-threaded scaling for intensive workloads, avoiding external disk latency. However, lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses requires dedicated network configuration, and the absence of discrete GPUs limits hardware-accelerated machine learning workloads to CPU-only execution. The instance is suited for high-concurrency databases, large-scale software compilation, distributed caching nodes, batch ETL operations, and data-intensive backend web serving.
